actor: Open-source vector database core maintainer setting network-security defaults
job: Decide to convert the post-CVE ports-closed, auth-on runbook advice into a shipped fail-closed bind default across the next release cycle.
outcome: A breaking default-change release refusing a non-loopback bind with no authentication credential, documented in the release notes rather than an optional hardening guide.
motivation: A 9.8 unauthenticated RCE with a named, internet-facing install base makes the shipped default, not the runbook, the maintainer's reputational obligation.

task.who: Core maintainers and networking-defaults owners on the project's steering group
task.what: Adopt fail-closed bind as a breaking release default
task.where: The project's release roadmap and default server configuration
task.why: Only a shipped default reaches operators skipping hardening pages
task.how: The Redis and MongoDB protected-mode precedent

job: Implement the startup guard that refuses a routable bind carrying no credential, downgrades it to loopback, or gates it behind explicit acknowledgement.
outcome: Server code that refuses a non-loopback bind without authentication, downgrades to loopback, or requires an explicit acknowledgement before starting.
motivation: Perimeter hygiene failed because thousands of RAG instances reached public IPs; only an in-process check stops the next exposed store.

task.what: Add a production check refusing routable bind without credential
task.where: The server bootstrap and interface-binding code path
task.why: In-process enforcement outlasts perimeter hygiene operators forget
task.how: Loopback default bind plus a fail-closed startup assertion

actor: Open-source vector database release manager and release-notes owner
job: Sequence the fail-closed default into a versioned release and document it as a breaking default change, not an optional hardening note.
outcome: Release notes that record the auth-on bind default as a breaking change, distinguishing it from an optional hardening guide operators ignore.
motivation: A default buried as optional hardening never reaches upgrade-averse operators, so only a flagged breaking change forces the safe configuration.

task.what: Document the auth-on bind default as a breaking change
task.where: The versioned release notes and upgrade migration guide
task.why: Breaking-change framing forces the safe default on upgraders
task.how: Semantic-version major bump with a documented migration path

job: Turn the 9.8 CVE and named internet-facing install base into a buyer's checklist item demanding auth-on-by-default from vector store vendors.
outcome: A procurement requirement that rejects vector stores lacking a fail-closed bind default, creating the demand that sets the maintainers' shipping schedule.
motivation: A retrieval-layer breach reconstructs the private text fed to the models, so buyers make the shipped default a purchasing precondition.

task.what: Require auth-on-by-default as a vector store purchasing criterion
task.where: Vendor security questionnaires and RAG platform procurement checklists
